summary: This Docker Compose configuration defines two services: a Docusaurus documentation builder that mounts your local code and node_modules into a container, and a LanguageTool service for spell-checking. The Docusaurus service uses build arguments to customize paths and user IDs, while LanguageTool runs as a persistent service with Java memory settings and a shared ngrams volume for language data.

explanations.9: The ${APP_HOME:-/opt/docusaurus} syntax means 'use the APP_HOME environment variable if it's set, otherwise default to /opt/docusaurus' — the :- part provides a fallback value.
explanations.12: This sets which user and group the container runs as using those same variables with defaults, written as user_id:group_id (like a Unix file permission).
explanations.16: The .. mounts the parent directory of this docker-compose file into the container at the APP_HOME path, so your source code is accessible inside.
explanations.17: This creates a named volume that persists node_modules between container runs, avoiding the need to reinstall dependencies every time.
explanations.19: The 'sleep infinity' command keeps the container running indefinitely so you can execute other commands inside it; without this, the container would exit immediately.
explanations.22: This references a pre-built Docker image from Docker Hub (erikvl87 is the username, languagetool is the image name).
explanations.25: This tells the LanguageTool Java application where to find grammar rule files; the /ngrams path is inside the container and maps to the named volume defined below.
